structured_output.analysis: The budget is effectively full: 84617/26880 works out to the same 3.148 average bits as iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e). So any per-layer upgrade has to be paid for with a downgrade. For the top loss layers, the knapsack already picked the better of the gptq and rht variants at the same bit width. For example, 27.up_proj uses gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) against rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00774 (E8972491007e7). The records give no cheap layer to downgrade. The gap between predicted and measured KL (0.398 vs 0.436) points to errors that build up across layers, which an algorithm option change can reduce at zero bit cost. I am trying the GPTQ options act_order and damp, which change no stored bits.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: No layer methods change, so the bits match iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e). Most of the loss sits in GPTQ-family MLP layers, e.g. 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065). Their activation kurtosis is high, e.g. 1090.09 (E24beed188b6a) and 146.379 (Ef95b39c759fb). Setting act_order=true makes GPTQ quantize the high-activation columns first, at no bit cost.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Same bits as iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e). Adds act_order=true and lowers damp from the default 0.01 to damp=0.005, so the Hessian correction is weighted more heavily. The target is layers like 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5) and 2.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E9baa10763ebe).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp02
proposals.rationale: Same bits as iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e). Tests act_order=true with a stronger damp=0.02. The idea is to curb overfitting to the 8x512 calibration set, given that measured KL (0.436) is above the predicted 0.398. Target layers include 27.gate_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00499 (Efa0bb391da67).
